newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Crew of damaged Mir station fine, slept in turns.
newsitem.headline: Crew of damaged Mir station fine, slept in turns.

text.p: The crew of the damaged Russian Mir space station were feeling fine after a "normal" night, a Mission Control spokeswoman said on Friday.

She told reporters that U.S. astronaut Michael Foale, mission commander Vasily Tsibliyev and flight engineer Alexander Lazutkin of Russia took turns in sleeping but offered no immediate explanation why this had been necessary.

"The night passed normally," the spokeswoman told reporters at the Korolyov Mission Control Centre near Moscow. "According to the latest radio contact, which took place about 20 minutes ago, the crew feel all right."
On Wednesday, an unmanned Progress cargo ship hit the 11-year-old Mir station during a training exercise and pierced a hole in one of its modules, which is now sealed off.

The collision smashed one of Mir's solar panels. Combined with the loss of the module, this has cut electric power by 25 to 30 percent in the whole station and forced the crew to halt experiments and physical exercise to save energy.
The cosmonauts now have to wait nearly two weeks for another Progress freighter to deliver repair supplies.
